data.q: Which type implements the http.Handler interface?
data.e: The Handler interface requires a ServeHTTP method with signature ServeHTTP(ResponseWriter, *Request). A struct with this method satisfies the interface.

data.q: What does http.HandleFunc register the handler with?
data.e: http.HandleFunc registers the handler function with the DefaultServeMux, the default HTTP request multiplexer.

data.q: Which function starts an HTTP server listening on a given address using the DefaultServeMux?
data.e: http.ListenAndServe starts a server on the given address using DefaultServeMux if handler is nil. http.Serve accepts a listener.

data.q: How do you create an HTTP request with an associated context for cancellation?
o: http.Request{Context: ctx, Method: method, URL: url}
data.e: http.NewRequestWithContext is the idiomatic way to create a request with a context since Go 1.13.

data.q: Which method on http.Client executes an HTTP request and returns a Response?
data.e: Do is the core method that sends the request and returns a Response. Get and Post are convenience wrappers.

data.q: What is the correct way to write an HTTP status code and headers before the response body?
data.e: Headers must be set before WriteHeader. WriteHeader sends the status line and headers; after that, headers cannot be changed.

data.q: Which package provides utilities for testing HTTP handlers without a network listener?
data.e: httptest provides NewRecorder, NewServer, and other helpers for testing HTTP code in-process.

data.q: How do you serve static files from a directory under a URL prefix?
data.e: StripPrefix removes the prefix before the FileServer sees the request path, otherwise the prefix becomes part of the filesystem path.

data.q: Which Server fields configure timeouts to defend against slow clients?
data.e: ReadTimeout, WriteTimeout, and IdleTimeout are the standard server timeout fields. IdleTimeout defaults to ReadTimeout if not set.

data.q: What status code does http.Redirect use by default if not specified?
data.e: http.Redirect defaults to 302 Found. Use http.StatusMovedPermanently (301) or http.StatusTemporaryRedirect (307) explicitly for other behaviors.

data.q: How do you set a cookie on an HTTP response?
data.e: http.SetCookie serializes the *http.Cookie and adds the Set-Cookie header. It handles escaping and multiple cookies correctly.

data.q: Which method gracefully shuts down an http.Server without disrupting active connections?
data.e: Shutdown gracefully stops the server, waiting for idle connections and optionally active requests (via context). Close closes listeners immediately.

data.q: What does the http.MaxBytesReader function do?
o: Limits the size of the response body written by the handler
Limits the size of the incoming request body
Limits the number of concurrent requests
data.e: MaxBytesReader wraps the request body reader to enforce a maximum byte limit, returning an error if exceeded. Useful for preventing DoS via large uploads.
